matches.rationale: GT1 concerns fabricated references [7, 37] in the Introduction about fairness and safety surveys. None of the findings address citation integrity or reference fabrication issues.

GT2 describes contradictory LayerCast method descriptions regarding whether upcasting happens 'just in time' or globally. Finding 2 identifies the exact same contradiction in Section 4 step (3), noting it conflicts with the Abstract, other parts of Section 4, and Appendix H regarding when FP32 computation occurs.

GT3 concerns unrealistic 0% Std@Acc claims for LayerCast in Appendix Table 26. Finding 1 addresses a different table (Table 23) with a copy-paste error between models, not LayerCast reproducibility claims.

GT4 describes FP32 OOM issues preventing fair comparison across configurations, specifically mentioning Qwen3-32B on 2 L40S GPUs. Finding 4 identifies a mismatch between the text claiming '4 GPUs with batch size 32' OOM and Table 10 showing OOM only in 2x L40S configurations, addressing the same experimental asymmetry issue.

GT5 concerns the Abstract's narrow attribution of variability solely to floating-point non-associativity, ignoring other GPU-level sources. None of the findings address this claim interpretation issue in the Abstract.

GT6 concerns hyperbolic language in the Conclusion about LayerCast achieving 'FP32-level determinism while maintaining reasonable memory efficiency.' None of the findings address rhetorical overselling in the Conclusion.
GT7 concerns the omission of environmental/energy cost discussion in the Appendix's societal impacts section. None of the findings address ethical or environmental considerations.

GT8 describes a contradiction in the Introduction between asserting fixed seeds ensure determinism and showing empirical nondeterminism. None of the findings address this specific logical inconsistency about seed determinism assumptions.
GT9 concerns cherry-picking or excluding BF16 catastrophic failure data points in variance tables. None of the findings identify missing or excluded extreme variance cases in the reported tables.

GT10 concerns oversimplified attribution of BF16 variance to mantissa bits, ignoring probability distribution interactions. None of the findings address this claim interpretation issue in the variance analysis.

GT11 concerns lack of justification for sample sizes (4, 16, 64 runs) and missing confidence intervals in random sampling experiments. None of the findings address statistical rigor or sample size justification issues.

GT12 concerns unclear relationship between random seed control and numerical precision effects in Section 2 Preliminaries. None of the findings address conceptual confusion in the Preliminaries section about determinism definitions.

GT13 concerns overstated language in the Introduction about nondeterminism 'posing a serious problem' without acknowledging mitigation strategies. None of the findings address rhetorical exaggeration in problem framing.

GT14 describes unexplained contradictions where FP32 occasionally shows higher variance than BF16 (Table 5, AIME'24, n=64). None of the findings identify this specific cross-section inconsistency in variance patterns.
GT15 concerns omission of limitations discussion (model size, architecture, hardware diversity) in Appendix A. None of the findings address missing scope limitations or generalizability caveats.
GT16 concerns Figure 1 caption incorrectly stating 960 rhombi (doubled from correct 480) to exaggerate BF16 instability. None of the findings address numerical errors in Figure 1 or its caption.

GT17 concerns use of different random seeds across greedy decoding runs despite claims of fixed seeds. None of the findings identify seed variation or stochasticity confounds in the experimental protocol.
GT18 concerns overgeneralization in Related Work claiming prior studies 'fully failed' to recognize numerical precision impacts. None of the findings address misrepresentation of prior literature.

GT19 describes contradiction between Table 1 showing similar BF16/FP16 rounding errors (~-0.00012) and experiments showing markedly different variance. None of the findings identify this cross-section inconsistency between Preliminaries and experimental results.

GT20 concerns missing LayerCast implementation details (non-linear layers, normalization, activation treatment). While Finding 2 addresses LayerCast contradictions, it focuses on the logical inconsistency of the described mechanism, not missing implementation details for reproducibility.
